article_title: Situational judgement testing at different stages of undergraduate medical training and the risk of professionalism lapses: A cohort study.
citation: Sahota G, Tiffin PA, Smith D, Tyrrell E, Hampshire M, Taggar J. (2026). Situational judgement testing at different stages of undergraduate medical training and the risk of professionalism lapses: A cohort study. Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1111/medu.70020
title: Administer professionalism SJTs during training rather than before admission, with professionalism-specific content and low cognitive load
description: The article's policy implication is that traditionally designed SJT-format assessments work better as developmental and selection tools during, not before, medical training. It states that "SJTs designed with professionalism‐specific content and a low cognitive load are those most likely to demonstrate incremental predictive validity over existing academic metrics", and that care should be taken to reduce cognitive load so scores add value above academic ability.
requirements: SJT content mapped to the professionalism curriculum or standards being assessed
cognitive load low enough that scores are not redundant with academic and cognitive metrics
constraints: Findings come from a single institution, so the authors advise caution in generalising to other settings
the evidence for construct-driven pre-admission SJTs as alternatives is not yet established
examples: The Nottingham Medical School administered a mandatory summative professionalism SJT at the end of second year, which independently predicted lapse odds in this cohort
key_sources: Sahota G, Tiffin PA, Smith D, Tyrrell E, Hampshire M, Taggar J. (2026). Situational judgement testing at different stages of undergraduate medical training and the risk of professionalism lapses: A cohort study. Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1111/medu.70020

article_title: Evaluation of Situational Judgment Tests in student selection in Indonesia and the impact on diversity issues.
citation: Soemantri Diantha, Findyartini Ardi, Yolanda Sophie, Morley Emma, Patterson Fiona. (2022). Evaluation of Situational Judgment Tests in student selection in Indonesia and the impact on diversity issues. BMC Medical Education, 22:239. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-022-03247-4
title: Staged SJT development process: specification, faculty item writing, concordance, psychometric evaluation, piloting
description: A reusable multi-stage process for building a selection SJT: define a test specification from curriculum analysis, faculty scenario writing with cross-writer evaluation, an expert concordance stage to set the scoring key, initial psychometric evaluation with students, then pilot testing with applicants. The article states development "started by defining the test specification, which outlines key aspects such as the non-academic domains to be assessed, the test length and the context within which scenarios are set."
requirements: Item writers drawn from faculty coordinating educational courses, student counselling, or teaching empathy, communication and professionalism
Psychometric item analysis against difficulty and discrimination thresholds before pilot testing
constraints: Scenarios and responses must be checked to be free from cultural, ethnicity and gender biases
target_learners: high school leaver applicants to undergraduate medical school
target_learning_goals: reliable assessment of non-academic attributes for admission selection
examples: 112 initial scenarios were reduced through the concordance stage and psychometric evaluation to 30 scenarios (128 items) selected for pilot testing
key_sources: Soemantri Diantha, Findyartini Ardi, Yolanda Sophie, Morley Emma, Patterson Fiona. (2022). Evaluation of Situational Judgment Tests in student selection in Indonesia and the impact on diversity issues. BMC Medical Education, 22:239. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-022-03247-4
